title: Layout with Display and Positioning
description: Learning how to control layout using the display property and different positioning methods in CSS.

flashcards.question: What does the CSS display property do?
flashcards.answer: It specifies how an element is displayed on the page, such as block, inline, or none.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between block and inline elements?
flashcards.answer: Block elements take full width and start on a new line; inline elements flow within text and take only necessary width.

flashcards.question: Name four common display property values.
What does position: static mean?
flashcards.answer: It is the default positioning; elements follow the normal document flow.

flashcards.question: How does position: relative affect an element?
flashcards.answer: It positions the element relative to its normal position, allowing offset using top, right, bottom, and left.

flashcards.question: What is position: absolute?
flashcards.answer: It positions the element relative to the nearest positioned ancestor or the initial containing block if none exist.

flashcards.question: What does position: fixed do?
flashcards.answer: Positions the element relative to the viewport, so it stays fixed during scrolling.

flashcards.question: How is position: sticky different from other position values?
flashcards.answer: It toggles between relative and fixed based on the scroll position.

flashcards.question: Can an element with display: none take up space on the page?
flashcards.answer: No, it is removed from the document flow and takes up no space.

flashcards.question: Which positioning property allows stacking of elements using z-index?
flashcards.answer: position (relative, absolute, fixed, or sticky) combined with the z-index property.
